points.why: It says the reviewer checks against guidelines and can judge tone, structure and formatting but cannot see the current UI, so a stricter prompt only tightens what it already checks.
It proposes tying articles to product areas, re-verifying them when a release touches those areas, and walking the steps in a staging build with an agent or script.
It gates destructive articles to a human or a verified walkthrough, but never names the agent-to-agent-to-publish path with no human in it or recommends mapping who reviews what.
It questions what the 98% means and proposes measuring it with seeded errors, but never restates it as 'nothing this reviewer can see is wrong.'

pitfalls.why: It explicitly rejects the prompt tweak as the whole fix and treats it as an optional small extra.
